headline: No shared I/O or write surfaces: prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are blocked by both profiles' read-only, no-egress defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable open-source list with no I/O surfaces, and Agent B has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces. With no shared channel or ingestion path, there is no plausible prompt-injection bridge between them.
conditions: IF either agent is wrapped in a shared clipboard or message-queue bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF a new orchestrator feeds one agent's raw output into the other, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard workflows.
Do not add an MCP server or shared message bus.
Review any wrapper that copies outputs between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent has network egress, and B cannot read or write the filesystem. A also exposes no data classes touched. Without shared storage or outbound transport, there is no credible data-leakage path between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to shared sensitive data, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, outbound exfiltration becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting shared sensitive workspaces.
Confirm B remains read-only and fileless.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling any shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surfaces, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Since neither can mutate a shared resource, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not place them on the same writable workspace.
Avoid shared git repositories.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if write access is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can only provide static repository guidance, and B is a game-playing agent with no browser, shell, or filesystem actions. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to treat A's text as authoritative; that pathway is not present in the profiles, so risk is limited.
conditions: IF an external controller starts executing B actions directly from A's text, cascade risk increases.
IF A's outputs are used as unverified facts in a downstream workflow, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on A's outputs.
Do not auto-feed A into B as instructions.
Log any downstream use of A's text.
requires-engineering: add verification gates for any future orchestration.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. With no identified regulated data flow, there is no residency, retention, or certification mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy, check residency and retention then.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document that neither agent processes PHI/PII.
Review retention settings if logs are added.
requires-engineering: add policy controls before introducing sensitive data.
